title: Testing the design guide — which made-up pages, and how the test runs

steps.intro: Each one is a page YouCoded does not have. Fresh builders who know only the guide design it; you critique; we fix the guide. Pick the ones worth testing — a mix of kinds tests more of the guide.

steps.headline: Which settings-style pages should the builders design?
steps.today: None of these exist. Settings pages are where most of the guide's rules about rows, switches, cards and labels apply.
steps.problem: If the guide's settings rules have gaps, a builder who has only the guide will fall into them here first.
steps.proposal: Pick any. Each becomes one page a builder designs from the guide alone.

options.label: Scheduled tasks
options.summary: Have the assistant do something on a schedule, like summarising your email every morning: a list of tasks, each with a time, an on/off switch, edit and delete.
pros: Tests lists, switches, a time picker, and a delete confirmation all at once.
cons: Close to the existing Specialists page, so it may test less that's new.

options.label: What the assistant remembers
options.summary: A page listing facts the assistant has saved about you, with search, edit, remove and "forget everything".
pros: Tests a long list, search, an empty page, and a scary red action.
cons: Mostly one list, so fewer kinds of control.

options.label: Spending limits
options.summary: A monthly cap per paid provider, how much is used so far, and a warning when you're close.
pros: Tests numbers, progress bars, warnings, and the money-orange colour rule.
cons: Number-heavy pages are rare in YouCoded, so the lessons may not carry far.

steps.path: Popups opened from somewhere in the app
steps.headline: Which popups or step-by-step flows should the builders design?
steps.today: None of these exist. Popups are where we spent most of this round's decisions (one-job card, buttons stacked, the ✕).
steps.problem: Those rules are new, so they're the likeliest to be worded in a way a newcomer misreads.
steps.proposal: Pick any. Each becomes one popup or flow, including its waiting and failed states.

options.label: Share a conversation
options.summary: Make a read-only link to a chat, choose whether files are included, copy the link, stop sharing later.
pros: Tests the one-job popup, a choice, a copy button, and undoing.
cons: Small, so it may pass easily.

options.label: Import from ChatGPT
options.summary: Pick your exported file, see what will come in, watch it import, and see what to do if part of it fails.
pros: Tests several steps, progress, and how errors are shown — a hard area.
cons: The biggest of the set; takes the builder longest.

options.label: Connect a calendar
options.summary: Sign in to Google Calendar, choose what the assistant may do (read only, or add events), and disconnect.
pros: Tests sign-in states and permission choices, which many future features will need.
cons: Overlaps with the existing Connected accounts page.

steps.surface: Made-up full pages and chat cards
steps.path: A page of its own, or a card inside a chat
steps.headline: Which full pages or in-chat cards should the builders design?
steps.today: None of these exist. The guide also covers whole pages and the cards that appear inside a conversation.
steps.problem: Those are the parts of the guide we've tested least this round.

options.label: Reading list
options.summary: A page of links and files you've saved for later, with tags, search, an empty state, and "ask the assistant about this".
pros: Tests a whole page: header, list, empty state, tags.

options.label: Study quiz card
options.summary: A card in the chat where the assistant quizzes you: a question, answer choices, right/wrong, and a score.
pros: Tests in-chat cards, which the guide covers less.
cons: Chat cards have their own redesign coming (permission prompts), so the lessons may be overtaken.

options.label: Notifications
options.summary: A panel listing what happened while you were away: finished tasks, mentions, updates, with mark-as-read.
pros: Tests a dropdown panel and read/unread looks.
cons: Hard to judge without real notifications behind it.

steps.prompt: e.g. a recipe planner, a habit tracker… or leave blank
steps.headline: Any made-up pages of your own you'd like in the set?
steps.today: The pages above are my suggestions.
steps.problem: You know which kinds of pages YouCoded is likely to grow next better than I do.
steps.proposal: Type any ideas, one short line each. Leave it blank if the picks above are enough.

steps.intro: Each round: fresh builders design the pages, you critique them on a review page, I change the guide, and the next round starts from scratch.

steps.path: What each builder is allowed to look at
steps.headline: Should builders see only the guide, or also a few real YouCoded screens?
steps.today: When I build a screen for real, I read the guide AND look at two or three existing screens that do a similar job.
steps.problem: Real screens fill in what the guide leaves out, so a builder who copies them can hide a gap in the guide.
steps.proposal: Either way, each builder gets the guide, the app's building blocks (buttons, switches, cards…) and the tool that photographs screens — nothing from our conversations.

options.label: Guide only
pros: Every mistake points straight at something the guide doesn't say — the fastest way to improve it.
Recommended because finding the guide's gaps is the whole point.
cons: The first round will look rougher than real work would.

options.label: Guide plus real screens
pros: Matches how real work is done, so results predict real quality.
cons: Builders may copy a screen instead of following the guide, so gaps stay hidden.

steps.headline: Same pages every round, or new ones?
steps.problem: Rebuilding the same pages shows whether the guide got better; but the guide could then be tuned to those pages alone.
steps.proposal: Pick how each round's set is made.

options.label: Same set plus one new
pros: You can compare round to round on the same pages.
The new page each round catches a guide that only works for the old ones — why I recommend it.
cons: One extra page to review each round.

options.label: All new each round
pros: Never tuned to particular pages.
cons: Hard to tell if a round got better because of the guide or because the pages were easier.

options.label: Same set only
pros: The cleanest comparison and the least to review.
cons: The guide may end up fitted to these few pages.

steps.path: Which AI model builds the pages
steps.headline: Which model should the builders be?
steps.today: Real YouCoded screens are built by the same model I am (Opus).
steps.problem: A cheaper model costs less per round but makes more of its own mistakes, which can be confused with the guide's.

options.label: Opus, like real work
pros: Mistakes are the guide's, not the model's — why I recommend it.
Predicts real sessions.
cons: Each round costs more of your usage.

options.label: Sonnet, cheaper
pros: About a fifth of the cost per round.
A guide a smaller model can follow is a very clear guide.
cons: Some misses will be the model, and I'd have to tell those apart.

steps.headline: Should each design come with the builder's own note on where the guide left it guessing?
steps.today: Review pages show pictures with my notes; builders don't add their own.
steps.problem: Some of a builder's mistakes are guesses where the guide was silent; you can't see those from the picture alone.
steps.proposal: Yes: under each design, a short "the guide didn't tell me…" list from its builder, which I'd use alongside your critique. No: you judge the pictures only.
